Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:168009
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 34522 of 2023

Applicant :- Khajan Singh
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Pramod Kumar Pandey,Sanjeev Kumar Khare

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Manoj Kumar Tripathi,Vinod Kumar Tirpathi
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1. Heard Sri Sanjeev Kumar Khare, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Manoj Kumar Tripathi,
learned counsel for the complainant (O.P. No. 2) and Sri Imran Khan, learned Aga for the
State-respondent.
2.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Complaint Case No. 02 of 2017, under Sections 323, 417, 376 IPC & 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station- Kotwali Shahar,
District- Bijnor, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. On 13.02.2017 an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was moved against applicant and his brother by O.P. No. 2, which was treated by court concerned as criminal complaint and as per the complaint dated 13.02.2017, applicant under the false promise of marriage made physical relationship with the complainant and his brother also sexually exploited the daughter of the complainant aged about 17 years and thereafter applicant and his brother refused to marry with them.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegation of sexual exploitation made against the applicant and his brother in the application under section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was totally false and baseless and neither applicant nor his brother ever sexually exploited either to the victim or her sister.

5. He further submitted that in the complaint there is no allegation against the applicant that he ever committed rape with the sister of the complainant but when statement of the complainant was recorded under Section 200 Cr.P.C. then complainant started making allegation that applicant sexually exploited her under the false promise of marriage and also committed rape with her sister and similar statement was given by sister of the complainant in her statement recorded under Section 202 Cr.P.C. and this fact clearly suggests that subsequently during the course of recording the statements under Sections 200 Cr.P.C. and 202 Cr.P.C. a new story was developed only to increase the seriousness of the matter.

6. He further submitted that applicant before the court concerned moved an application under Section 245(2) Cr.P.C. for his discharge but when his discharge was dismissed then he approached before this Court vide Criminal Misc. Application under Section 482 No. 37079 of 2019 and on 14.10.2019 co-ordinate Bench of this Court referred the matter to the mediation centre and proceeding pending against the applicant was kept in abeyance but in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in case of Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency Private Limited and Another v. Central Bureau of Investigation (2018) 16 SCC 299, coercive measures were taken against the applicant and thereafter applicant was arrested on 12.07.2023.
7.

entities.text: Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency Private Limited and Another v. Central Bureau of Investigation (2018) 16 SCC 299
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He further submitted that admittedly complainant of the case is a major girl and from her statement recorded under Section 200 Cr.P.C., her consent is apparent and applicant is detained in jail in a complainant case, therefore, applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
8.

Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the complainant (O.P. No. 2) opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that there is allegation of sexual exploitation against the applicant and applicant not only sexually exploited the complainant but also committed rape with her minor sister but could not dispute the fact that applicant was summoned in a complaint case and when he approached this Court in Criminal Misc. Application Under Section 482 No. 37079 of 2019 then initially proceeding pending against him was stayed by this Court.

9. They further could not dispute the fact that complainant is a major girl and she appears to be consenting party and she did not make any allegation of rape against the applicant with regard to her sister in the complaint dated 13.02.2017.
10. I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. From the record, it reflects that applicant was summoned in the present matter along with his brother in a complaint case and vide order dated 14.10.2019 proceeding of the complaint case was stayed by this Court but subsequently on the basis of law laid down by the Apex Court in case of Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency Private Limited (supra) coercive measures were taken against the Khajan Singh vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110226058/
2 applicant and he was arrested.
12.

sentences.text:
From the record, it also reflects that complainant i.e. O.P. No. 2 is a major girl and she appears to be consenting party and although, in her statement recorded under Section 200 Cr.P.C. she also made allegation against the applicant that applicant also committed rape with her sister aged about 17 years and when statement of her sister was recorded under Section 202 Cr.P.C. then she also stated that applicant committed rape with her but this fact has not been mentioned by the complainant in the complaint dated 13.02.2017.
13.

Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
14. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

15. Let the applicant- Khajan Singh be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
16.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

17. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
